question.stem: Which of the following information should the nurse include?
question.preamble: The nurse in a community-based setting is teaching clients over 65 years of age about health promotion activities.

options.text: “Purchase all of your prescribed medications at the same pharmacy.”
“Schedule an appointment for a vision screening every 3 years.”
“Participate in daily aerobic exercises for 60 minutes.”

question.explanation: Using a single pharmacy (Option 1) allows the pharmacist to screen all of a client's medications together for interactions and duplications, an important safety measure for older adults. Vision screening (Option 2) should generally occur annually for this age group, not every 3 years. Recommending 60 minutes of daily aerobic exercise (Option 3) exceeds standard general guidelines (about 150 minutes per week of moderate activity) and may not be realistic or safe as a blanket recommendation. Increasing fat-soluble vitamin intake (Option 4) is not a general health-promotion recommendation, and excess fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) can accumulate to toxic levels.
